claim: Preschoolers (mean 54 months) isolate variables mainly when the evidence is ambiguous: informative intervention 1/20 with unambiguous evidence vs 9/20 and 10/20 with ambiguous evidence (Exp 1), and 1/20 vs 9/20 when they had to invent the test (Exp 2). Play variety did not differ. Full text re-read confirms the cell counts (Exp 1 N=60, chi2 8.53 and 10.16; Exp 2 N=40). No direct replication was found; Moeller et al. 2022 (N=57, ages 3-6) is a conceptual follow-up in a different paradigm.
agent_test: none; this is a child result. Adult-style analogue: show the agent clear vs ambiguous prior evidence and count how often it designs a discriminating test.

claim: The Cook et al. 2011 result is a qualitative fit to EIG, not a fit of computed EIG to individual children; authors disclaim that children understand why isolation works. Cells are small (N=20), the world has 2-4 variables, and 55% of children in the ambiguous condition still did not do it. Moeller et al. 2022 found that recognising confounded evidence and choosing a controlled test were unrelated, so Cook's pattern need not reflect understanding.
agent_test: none; use as a caution that the developmental case licenses the idea, not the numbers.

claim: Humans choose queries in ways that track EIG-like value in many tasks, but the competing measures (information gain, KL, probability gain) usually agree, so most data cannot tell them apart.
agent_test: Log cases where EIG and probability gain disagree and see which better predicts final correctness at equal tokens.

claim: In experience-based tasks people favoured the higher probability-gain feature (82-97% of subjects, median 99% of trials), not information gain; with verbally described statistics the preference fell to 27-30% in two conditions. EIG is not the only or best human model.
agent_test: Compare EIG-ranked vs probability-gain-ranked query choice on the agent's own tasks.

claim: Under time pressure people shift from EIG toward a positive-testing heuristic; positive testing is not an approximation of EIG. Humans are poor at generating high-EIG questions but good at choosing among supplied ones (generation vs recognition gap).
agent_test: Give the agent a cheap list of candidate tests and a ranking step instead of asking for one best test directly.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human Battleship questions average 1.27 bits of EIG (best 3.61; 97% above zero). One raw GPT-4 or CodeLlama-7b sample averages 0.65-0.66 bits; sampling k=5 questions and keeping the highest-EIG one matches humans and k=10 beats them (p<.001).
agent_test: Sample k candidate tests, compute EIG in code, ask the best; compare with k=1 at equal tokens on a Battleship-like or hidden-rule task.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: On 20 Questions, choosing each question by EIG computed in code over LLM-sampled hypotheses raises success by 37.4 percentage points on average (never lower), e.g. GPT-4o Animals 45 -> 93, Mistral-Large Celebrities 19 -> 91, Llama-3.1-8B Things 10 -> 26.
agent_test: Replicate in our harness: prompt-only vs EIG-in-code at equal total tokens (count the extra likelihood calls).

claim: Letting the model itself pick the best question from the same candidates (implicit maximisation) recovers only part of the gain: Animals GPT-4o 70 vs 93, Mistral-Large 53 vs 95, Qwen 61 vs 95 (Prompt-Only 45/33/45). Code-side arithmetic is what matters.
agent_test: Arm A: LLM picks the best test. Arm B: code scores candidates by EIG. Same candidates, equal tokens.

claim: The belief state must be kept as sampled hypotheses filtered against the answer history. Raw in-context beliefs fail: Animals GPT-4o 25% vs 93% (Mistral 53 vs 95).
agent_test: Ablate hypothesis filtering: carry hypotheses forward unfiltered vs filtered against all observations.

claim: Full EIG beats marginal answer entropy and the even-split rule by a smaller margin than it beats prompting (Animals GPT-4o: 93 vs 88 vs 83; Celebrities Mistral: 91 vs 68 vs 63). Most of the gain comes from having a hypothesis set and scoring splits at all. At about the same wall-clock (BED 2h30m, Split 2h46m, Implicit Max 2h29m on Qwen2.5-72B) EIG still wins, e.g. Celebrities GPT-4o: 86 vs 63 (split) vs 50 (LLM picks best candidate).
agent_test: Test whether a cheap split-balance score (no noise model) gets most of the benefit at lower cost.

claim: Estimating uncertainty in answer space beats estimating it in hypothesis space: Data-Estimation Animals GPT-4o 70 vs 93, and it ran more than 10x slower (1d17h vs 2h30m for Qwen2.5-72B).
agent_test: Cost-account the EIG routine; reuse likelihood calls.

claim: EIG selection in the Uncertainty of Thoughts scaffold raises success over direct prompting by 38.1 percent on average (a relative figure, not points: e.g. GPT-4 DX 89.4 -> 97.0, Thing 30.8 -> 36.8, FloDial 42.5 -> 67.8), and it beats CoT-SC, Reflexion and ToT variants; at about 9k tokens UoT beats adapted ToT (20Q 54.4 vs 40.9).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison against best-of-N and ToT on a diagnosis-style task.

claim: EIG-based clarifying questions raise downstream accuracy on code tasks: HumanEval GPT-3.5 binary 70.8 -> 85.6; APPS GPT-4o-mini open 75.1 -> 87.2, binary 62.9 -> 75.3. Gains shrink for stronger models on easy tasks (HumanEval GPT-4o-mini binary 79.6 -> 81.5).
agent_test: Ask-before-solving step on underspecified coding items; measure accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Weighting sampled solutions by the LLM's own log-probabilities is worse than uniform weights (20 Questions rank score at t=10 on GPT-3.5: uniform 6.2 vs logprobs 4.1; higher is better). LLM probabilities are biased and overconfident; conformal set sizes are a more robust uncertainty signal.
agent_test: Compare uniform sample weights vs model-stated probabilities inside the EIG routine.

claim: Unaided LLMs are weak at informative questioning: GPT-4 wins 31% (Things) and 50% (Celebrities) of 20-question games, uses 17-18 of 20 turns; open models are under 25%; zero-shot questions average 0.29-0.35 of a perfect half-split.
agent_test: Baseline for any questioning arm; report mean turns and split quality.

claim: Training on EIG signals helps small models (DPO on high vs low EIG pairs: INLG 56.7 -> 68.9 success, Things 51.1 -> 61.1; Celebrities gain +1.1 only; plain fine-tuning lowers success; BigBench raised success but not EIG). Out of scope for a no-training scaffold.
agent_test: none; training result.

claim: Pairing LLM wording with explicit Bayesian design helps preference elicitation (OPEN beats LM-only in human arms of about 44 users; open-ended questions beat pairwise), but most gain came from using the Bayesian prediction, and exact TIDA values were not recorded.
agent_test: Low priority; needs a user-preference task.

claim: LLM-proposed rules plus information-gain experiment choice fit human Zendo behaviour better than a direct ReAct LLM (R2 .57 vs .25). Hard-rule variants score best on accuracy but fit humans worst. Row mapping resolved from Tables 1 and 3: Direct LLM 4.60, online fuzzy 5.35, online hard 6.55 of 8 (human 5.26). Choosing experiments: LLM-picked 4.72, random 5.84, InfoGain 6.55 (hard rules); a random proposer with 10 candidates equals an LLM proposer.
agent_test: Use hypothesis-revision plus EIG experiments on a rule-induction task; verify the table first.

claim: Unaided GPT-3 (2022) showed no directed exploration and failed intervention-based causal tasks, while doing well on described vignettes. No re-test with 2025-26 models was found.
agent_test: Re-run a horizon or blicket-type task on the current model with and without an EIG step.

claim: Models often cannot identify the one needed clarifying question even when they can solve the full problem: Logic-Q and Planning-Q at best about 50%, math word problems above 80%; CoT and few-shot help little; breadth-first search reaches 80.6% at depth 5 and 99.8% at depth 10. Models tested were 2024-early-2025 (o1-preview, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking); no number for o3, Claude extended thinking or Gemini 2.5.
agent_test: Use QuestBench as an equal-token test of an EIG or search step.

claim: Multi-turn degradation: models guess early and do not recover (39% average drop from single-turn to multi-turn over 200,000+ simulated conversations), which argues for deciding explicitly when to ask versus answer.
agent_test: Add an ask-or-answer gate scored by entropy over intents; test on underspecified tasks.

claim: Lookahead beats one-step EIG when a simulator of future answers exists (MCTS > greedy EIG in all cases), and greedy EIG beats base Llama-3.1-8B. The simulator needs meta-training.
agent_test: Test two-step lookahead in code vs greedy EIG at equal tokens.

claim: Children aged 7-8 mostly ask hypothesis-scanning questions; 9-11 and adults ask constraint-seeking ones. Primary numbers now read for Ruggeri et al. 2016 (hierarchical 20 questions: 4.92 / 4.38 / 3.36 questions for 7-year-olds / 10-year-olds / adults vs 2.85 optimal; mean question IG 0.83 vs 1.06 optimal vs 0.50 random). Nelson et al. 2014 is still abstract-only.
agent_test: Check whether agent questions are scanning-type (guess an item) early in a game.

claim: Positive testing in the Wason task is explained by EIG under a rarity assumption (Oaksford and Chater 1994), and Binz and Schulz found GPT-3 reproduces the congruence bias; the original paper was not opened.
agent_test: Not worth a test until the primary source is read.

claim: Reasoning mode lifts question quality for small open models but does not make them pick the best question: Qwen3-30B partially observable win rate 0.10 without thinking vs 0.93 with thinking (IG/turn 0.14 vs 0.42), yet the thinking model chose the max-IG candidate on only 25% of turns (Qwen3-8B 19%). No o-series, Claude or Gemini 2.5 number exists.
agent_test: Run the scaffold against a thinking model on the same task and log the share of turns where its chosen question equals the code-ranked best.

claim: Wasted questions have a measured cost in tool agents. Past a middle clarification budget success plateaus or falls and steps rise (24.2 -> 26.5 -> 25.1); a clarifier without an information target lowered success (Qwen3-8B clarifier: -3.5 points averaged for the Qwen3-8B agent, -6.3 on airline); a learned information-gain clarifier used 1.3 turns vs 3.9-5.1 and raised success +3.7 points over five backbones.
agent_test: Cap questions per task and log success vs number of questions asked.

claim: People over-ask when one hypothesis remains: 83% of 7-year-olds, 70% of 10-year-olds and 52% of adults asked at least one zero-information question. A stop rule is a separate component from question choice.
agent_test: Stop asking when the filtered hypothesis set has one member or max EIG is under a small threshold; measure zero-gain questions.

claim: Ask-or-answer gates are weak: entropy over simulated user intents reaches AUROC 0.63 on QA (GPT-3) and about 0.51-0.53 on translation; a gate trained on expected downstream outcome beat ProCoT prompting (F1 24.3 vs 15.6) but beat a random gate by about 1 F1 point. No head-to-head of entropy-over-intents vs expected gain minus cost exists.
agent_test: Compare three gates in our harness: always ask, intent-entropy threshold, EIG minus cost.

claim: The nearest equal-compute test favours code EIG: at about equal wall-clock it beats the plain split rule and 'LLM picks the best of the same candidates' in every Table 1 cell, but no paper compares it with best-of-N or extended thinking at equal tokens.
agent_test: Bench arm: EIG-code vs split vs best-of-N vs thinking model, equal total tokens.

claim: Cost of EIG: LLM calls are O(N+M+NM) for answer-by-LLM tasks but only O(N+M) when answers come from executing sampled solutions. BED-LLM's wall-clock was no higher than marginal entropy or split. In one turn the ranking of five candidates at 10 sampled hypotheses matched that at 85. Token counts are not reported.
agent_test: Count tokens per turn for N=5,10,20 and M=4,8 on one task.

claim: Open-task hypothesis generation has one working recipe, tested only on entities and preferences: one-list diverse sampling (T=1.3), history-compat filter (threshold 0.2), at least 5 survivors, uniform prior, re-ask 2-3 times; independent sampling of 200 collapses onto a few modes. No test on code, proofs or research questions.
agent_test: Try the recipe on a code-spec disambiguation task; track survivors per turn and rank stability.

claim: Negative result under a rate-limited search: no paper found comparing Shannon EIG with probability gain or expected error reduction in LLM agents, testing LLM likelihoods for tool outputs, or testing a noisy or wrong answerer beyond an LLM-to-LLM mismatch.
agent_test: Own bench arms: Shannon vs probability gain; answer-flip noise of 10/20/30%.
